_about: The study's register. Each rule is scored only on trades entered AFTER after_ts (out of sample); the study adds rules here and never edits an existing one's filter or after_ts. filter ops: < <= > >= == != on columns of data/abcd.csv; exit is the paper column to score (x_flow4 runner, x_h5 5-min, x_h3 3-min, x_h15, x_h5f14, x_t15s40).

strategies.note: sell at 3 minutes instead of 5 (from 84 post-fix trades: +10.1% vs +5.0%)
fewer than 65 wallets in the trigger minute (from 49 live coins: 72% win vs 38%)
one buyer took more than 10% of the trigger minute's buying (from 49 live coins: 75% win vs 36%)

study's own: A coins whose launch bundle was at most 3 wallets, runner exit. From 100 passed A trades: n33 +18.4% net, 76-85% win, 12% stopped vs n67 -9.0% net, 37-40% win; holds at the 5-s fill price (+13.9%), in 10 of 13 hours, and on D's coins (n27 +13.2% vs n53 -8.7%, mostly the same mints). Hypothesis until 40 out-of-sample trades.

study's own LAUNCH-TIME rule (score by hand from launches.csv, create_ts > after_ts): a tier-1 bundled launch (bundle 40-79% of supply, median dev buy 4.9 SOL, ~25 an hour), bought at the +4 s price (median MC $32K), sold at 5 min. 604 launches in 24 h: 5-min multiple median 1.24 on the 86% still trading, 44% above the 10% cost, 28% reached 5x and 16% 10x by 5 min, 55% graduated; positive in all six 4-hour blocks. The website's bundled-70%+ skip and S4's clean-launch premise point the other way. Not yet a book: needs the executor to see whether the +4 s price is obtainable (bundle sells into the buy) — judge on the next 24 h of launches first.

the owner's E trigger ($100K traded in 5 min, MC under $100K) sold at 5 minutes: the best E exit so far, +8.8% net on 31 passed trades (runner +5.3%, 1.5x/-40% -0.1%); 31 trades is too few to mean anything.
